accounting.rationale: Original physical PDF121, printed107, lines8-9 defines BIND capability for variables/common blocks. It is not a new no-op execution and does not require an associated C entity to exist;18.9.1p4 explicitly permits its absence.
PENDING source-use of the module-variable route through C819/C820 and18.9.1. A variable, a procedure, a derived type and a COMMON block do not share one declaration grammar.

PENDING the named COMMON route through R835/R836, C821 and18.9.1p3: all declarations keep the same binding label; members correspond to C structure components, or a single member can correspond to the C variable directly. The block's BIND does not give BIND to its member variables.

The attribute describes capability, not evidence that a chosen C declaration, link, layout or runtime actually interoperates. Source eligibility, selected companion/interface qualification and a multilang observation remain separate pending gates.

The described counterpart is a C variable, not a C function, type tag or arbitrary linker symbol.5.5.7 allows several kinds of companion mechanism and processor-dependent selection; do not assume an undocumented C-conforming compiler merely from the BIND(C) spelling.
The counterpart's name has external linkage. PENDING original18.9/19.5.1.5 source-use without equating a Fortran identifier, binding-label character value and platform symbol decoration.

18.9 supplies data/common interoperation and label rules. The existing S18_3_7_001_valid__c_interop procedure bridge and S7_3_2_2_003_valid__assumed_descriptor case retain their own subjects, inputs and roles, not new8.5.5 coverage.
PDF121 line10: C binding syntax and the optional, ordered, scalar default-character constant NAME expression.
PDF121 line11 retains all four permitted entity categories, not just the data subjects of the heading.
PDF121 line12 restricts the BIND variable's declaration context; it does not impose the same module-only rule on a BIND common block.
PDF121 line13 invokes the complete original18.3 variable/type/parameter criteria, not a successful Fortran compile or descriptor-wrapper acceptance.
PDF121 line14 applies to every member of the bound common block; do not test only the first or give BIND to individual members.
PDF121 lines15-16: a conditional companion-identifier restriction after removal of leading and trailing blanks. Empty/all-blank values are outside this nonzero-length premise.
The original single NOTE on PDF121 explains C universal character names and a default-CHARACTER representation limit; it is not a universal Unicode support obligation or another source requirement.
ISO/IEC9899:2018's universal-character-name facility is the stated example. A companion mechanism is not presumed to be an arbitrary installed C compiler.
C identifiers can involve characters beyond the C basic set. PENDING documentary name/repertoire mapping, not a fabricated C identifier or reserved-name test.

The particular Fortran processor's default-character representation might not contain those characters. R808 still requires a default-character NAME expression; nondefault CHARACTER, UTF-8 bytes, accepted source bytes or a display glyph are not substitutes.

In the stated representation-limited situation the C entity cannot be referenced from Fortran. Preserve this genuine documentary/interface limit without inventing an executable source string that cannot be represented.
PDF121 line17 contains the common-block SAVE implication and permission to confirm it explicitly. The permission is not a separate no-op program.

PENDING one explicit SAVE /block/ confirmation of the real retention context. C862 still excludes an explicit SAVE on an individual common member; C8123 excludes individual BIND on a common-block object. Module-variable SAVE has a different canonical source.

requirements.title: C language-binding syntax and the qualified NAME expression
requirements.definition: A language-binding-spec uses BIND with parenthesized C and optionally one following comma/NAME= specification. The NAME expression is scalar, default CHARACTER and constant. This grammar is reused in its permitted data/common/procedure consumers; the superficially similar BIND(C) type/ENUM forms retain their own syntax. The spelling C does not establish which actual companion mechanism was selected.

pending.c-token: PENDING complete module INTEGER(C_INT) variable declaration with BIND(D), repaired only by D to C, plus the correct C-token admission. Parentheses, entity count, variable context and interoperable type already hold; diagnose the language-binding grammar, not an unsupported companion implementation.
pending.without-name: PENDING BIND(C) compile admissions for one module INTEGER(C_INT) variable and a named COMMON block whose members are eligible. Omitted NAME is legal; default data/common label interpretation remains18.9.2 rather than a linker-symbol observation.
pending.literal-name: PENDING scalar default-character NAME='bind_item' in a one-entity module declaration and a one-block BIND statement. Positive syntax admission only; actual companion identifier acceptance and external linkage evidence remain separate.
pending.constant-name-expression: PENDING a prior default-CHARACTER PARAMETER and a constant concatenation producing bind_item, each used as NAME with otherwise identical valid context. Preserve constancy, scalar rank and default kind; do not infer a value from a mutable variable or compare a runtime label against the same conversion under test.
pending.empty-all-blank-name: PENDING syntax/source-use for NAME='' and NAME='   '. C802/C877 still see NAME as present. The nonzero identifier premise does not apply, and18.9.2 gives no binding label rather than a fallback to the default label.
pending.single-name-specifier: PENDING one valid data declaration with a second NAME= specification added inside the same BIND parentheses. Remove only the second specification for the repair; both individual expressions are otherwise valid. Do not credit an unrelated entity-list or duplicate outer BIND attribute error.
pending.name-order: PENDING otherwise valid BIND(NAME='bind_item',C), repaired solely by restoring C before the optional NAME field. Keep a complete module and one eligible variable; generic EOF/missing-END or wrong-source recovery is not a grammar oracle.
pending.scalar-name: PENDING NAME=['bind_item'] versus NAME='bind_item', removing only the array-constructor brackets for the repair. Both use default CHARACTER constants and a companion-qualified ordinary label; require the NAME expression's rank/category cause, not unsupported array syntax or label validity.
pending.character-name: PENDING an INTEGER named constant used as NAME, repaired by replacing the NAME expression with a scalar default-CHARACTER constant bind_item. All variable/BIND context predicates remain fixed; a generic kind or unsupported identifier message is not the intended type report.
pending.constant-name: PENDING module CHARACTER variable label initialized to bind_item but lacking PARAMETER, used as NAME. Repair only its declaration by adding PARAMETER; the binding's receiver and NAME value do not change. Initialization does not make a variable a constant expression.
pending.default-kind-name: PENDING supported-domain source plan for a scalar constant NAME of a genuinely supported nondefault CHARACTER kind, repaired to a default-character constant with the same qualified label. Establish kind support and distinctness first. No guessed kind code, unsupported-kind declaration, new profile or runtime IF hiding an invalid declaration.
pending.role-and-label-source-use: PENDING original-owner map of data type declarations, R835 BIND statements and R1531 procedure binding. Keep C802/C803 and C877 list/role conditions; R728 TYPE,BIND(C) and R760 ENUM,BIND(C) do not gain arbitrary NAME syntax. Data/common default, explicit case-sensitive, trimmed and absent-label meanings stay18.9.2; procedure exceptions stay18.10.2.

requirements.oracle: Qualified compile admissions and focused grammar/type/rank/constancy report-control contrasts. Planned negatives retain an otherwise conforming complete module, supported symbolic C_INT and one eligible receiver. Reporting capability is not mandatory fatal rejection or prescribed English wording.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source validity, companion identity/identifier rules and actual C interoperation are separate. C802/C803/C877 remain defining owners; no duplicate C801 work or new proof from keyword recognition. Reports must bind the real NAME/C-syntax property, subject and source location, excluding echoes, generic expected/kind strings, unsupported facilities, crashes, verifier/resource failures and recovery.

requirements.title: BIND is limited to the stated entity categories
requirements.definition: An entity with BIND is a common block, variable, type or procedure. This category restriction is not permission to use every BIND syntax on every category, to add BIND to named constants, or to ignore the category's own interoperability and declaration constraints.

pending.common-block-role: PENDING a named COMMON block bound by R835/R836, with INTEGER(C_INT) members and no individual member BIND. Compile admission only; a common-block name is not a variable name in a type declaration.
pending.module-variable-role: PENDING ordinary scalar and explicit-shape INTEGER(C_INT) module variables, using the type-declaration and separate BIND-statement routes. Preserve C819/C820; no statement that a Fortran compile proves the chosen C entity or ABI.
pending.derived-type-role: PENDING canonical R728 TYPE,BIND(C) context with one nonpointer nonallocatable INTEGER(C_INT) component, no SEQUENCE, parameters, EXTENDS or type-bound-procedure part. Preserve C1801-C1806; a type's BIND does not assign a global variable label to the type or automatically bind variables declared with it.
pending.procedure-role: PENDING a complete non-elemental interoperable procedure in proper procedure syntax, with an explicit interface where required. C803 still prohibits procedure names in a data type declaration carrying language-binding-spec. Procedure label, internal/dummy/pointer and submodule exceptions remain canonical; do not use the prohibited data spelling as its admission.
pending.named-constant-excluded: PENDING module INTEGER(C_INT),PARAMETER,BIND(C) n=1. Repair only removal of PARAMETER and its comma, retaining the initializer, BIND, module and type. The repaired entity is an ordinary interoperable variable; the negative must report the disallowed named-constant/category relation rather than a missing initializer or unsupported kind.
pending.enum-definition-role: PENDING source-use of R760: the ENUM,BIND(C) definition and its optional enum type are not BIND attributes on each INTEGER named enumerator. Enumeration types are a different noninteroperable category. No named-enum/enum-constant wrapper or KIND-of-enum probe.
pending.other-entity-source-use: PENDING finite source contrasts for module, namelist-group and abstract-interface names, preserving their actual grammars and roles. If a proposed spelling independently violates R835/R836 or another consumer, keep it documentary rather than claiming an isolated C818 negative.

requirements.oracle: Eligible category contexts and one focused named-constant-to-variable repair, with actual syntax and interoperability prerequisites. Other entity-role contrasts require independently isolated source before diagnostic authoring.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The four-category list is not a universal BIND constructor. No incomplete interface, prohibited elemental procedure, invalid derived type, common-member misuse or unrelated declaration recovery can corroborate this category condition.

requirements.title: A BIND variable is declared in a module specification-part
requirements.definition: A variable that has BIND is declared in the specification-part of a module. The rule applies to the variable entity, not to a bound common block as a whole. A contained procedure, BLOCK or submodule does not become a module specification-part merely through textual nesting or ancestry.

pending.submodule-local: PENDING an eligible ancestor declaring a separate module procedure and a complete matching submodule that declares a local BIND variable. Remove only that variable BIND for the repair. Preserve C1412 and matching interfaces; missing module artifacts or unsupported submodules are not this source condition.
pending.common-placement-source-use: PENDING R835 named-common bindings outside a module with otherwise eligible common members. C819 does not force those members to be module BIND variables; C8123 actually excludes individually bound common members. No scope-changing common/variable repair is substituted for a focused variable-context pair.
pending.interface-result-dummy-source-use: PENDING exact source/role map of interface bodies, function results and dummies against the module-variable route. Data-variable BIND and an enclosing procedure's proc-language-binding-spec are different. Hold compound cases until C803, C819 and procedure-variable conditions are disentangled.

requirements.oracle: Seven complete compile/f2023 fixtures represent module-admission, main-local, external-procedure-local and contained-procedure-local. A proper module specification-part admits one ordinary scalar INTEGER(C_INT),BIND(C) variable. Three negatives declare that same eligible variable in a main program, an external subroutine and a module-contained subroutine's own specification-part. Each control deletes only ', bind(c)', preserving every other byte, including the local entity, intrinsic USE, type, rank, executable assignment and complete outer context. Admission requires successful object compilation; the controls are positive-control evidence, not runtime effects. A negative requires an actual located BIND-variable/module-declaration-context report at its sole entity declaration. Ordinary zero/nonzero and specifically qualified nonfatal reporting may satisfy that capability; neither fatal rejection, a printed C819 code nor generic keyword output is required or sufficient.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Submodule placement, common-placement source-use and interface/result/dummy source-use remain pending. All six other 8.5.5 requirements and their plans are preserved. Prior intrinsic ISO_C_BINDING makes the guaranteed C_INT kind accessible in the actual declaring scope. Each variable is scalar, noncoarray, nonpointer, nonallocatable, nondummy and not a function result or named constant, with no initializer or duplicate binding. Under 18.3.1/18.3.5 its type and parameters are interoperable; 18.9.1p4 requires no associated C entity. No kind code, width, ABI, foreign counterpart, link, runtime retention, module SAVE or S8.5.5-002 effect is observed. Wrong entity/type/kind/attribute, missing module/interface, malformed declaration, source echo, bare BIND/module words, unsupported/unimplemented recovery, Internal/ASR/verifier, crash, resource and timeout failures are noncredit. A literal predicate without a supported causal report remains unqualified, not compiler-consensus proof. Source, fixture, observational-inventory and processor-mode qualification remain independent; generation preserves their administrative records without renewing them.

requirements.title: A BIND variable meets the original interoperability criteria
requirements.source: 8.5.5 C820, physical PDF121, printed107, line13; directed18.3
requirements.definition: A BIND variable is interoperable under18.3. Named scalars need interoperable type/parameters, no coarray, neither ALLOCATABLE nor POINTER, and the stated nonassumed/constant CHARACTER length. Named arrays require interoperable type/parameters, noncoarray status and explicit shape or assumed size, with the CHARACTER length conditions. These category criteria are distinct from compatibility with a particular C object, which has additional conditions such as nonzero array size.

pending.pointer-excluded: PENDING module scalar INTEGER(C_INT),POINTER,BIND(C) variable with no initializer or association use. Remove only POINTER for the repair. Require the scalar variable's forbidden POINTER/interoperability property, not an unassociated-value or unsupported facility error.
pending.allocatable-excluded: PENDING module scalar INTEGER(C_INT),ALLOCATABLE,BIND(C) variable with no initializer. Remove only ALLOCATABLE; a scalar avoids an independently invalid explicit-shape allocatable declaration. Do not read unallocated data or convert a descriptor-dummy example into this global-variable role.
pending.coarray-excluded: PENDING supported-configuration module INTEGER(C_INT) variable with explicit scalar coshape and BIND. Remove only its coshape for the repair; module SAVE and the ordinary coarray declaration conditions already hold. Coarray-disabled/unsupported diagnostics cannot count, and no new profile is authored.
pending.character-length-domain: PENDING only when C_CHAR denotes a supported CHARACTER kind: module CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=2) BIND variable, repaired only to LEN1. C_CHAR may be-1 under18.2.2; do not declare that value as a kind or count unsupported-kind failure as a length violation. The profile/interface premise remains explicit until independently established.
pending.derived-type-interoperability: PENDING ordinary module BIND variable of a prior derived type with one INTEGER(C_INT) component but without type BIND. Repair only by adding BIND(C) to that otherwise eligible type, which has no SEQUENCE, parameters, EXTENDS, default components or type-bound procedures. A future C structure partner needs corresponding component count/order/types; bit-fields, flexible array members and unions retain18.3.4p3's exclusion. Matching type/member names do not prove interoperability.
pending.type-kind-mapping-source-use: PENDING full Table18.2 intrinsic type/kind mapping inventory with the actual18.2.2 availability/sentinel rules, plus special C_PTR/C_FUNPTR and enum types under18.3.2/.3. C_PTR/C_FUNPTR objects are not Fortran POINTER variables. C_CHAR, C_BOOL, real/complex and additional integer mappings are not all guaranteed; a valid Fortran kind without an established C mapping needs genuine evidence, not a guessed code.
pending.deferred-assumed-parameter-source-use: PENDING exact scalar/array CHARACTER length and deferred-parameter source relations. C702 requires POINTER/ALLOCATABLE for deferred parameters, and other module/assumed-length rules can already exclude a candidate. Do not fabricate an isolated C820 deferred-length negative by silently adding multiple independent violations; keep the compound domain documentary.
pending.descriptor-route-boundary: PENDING source-use distinguishing BIND module data from BIND procedure dummies admitted under C1563-C1568 and18.3.7, including allocatable/pointer/assumed-shape/rank descriptor routes. Those procedure facilities do not waive18.3.5/.6 for global data. Preserve S7_3_2_2_003_valid__assumed_descriptor, its optional mapping profile and original selected-header qualification; no header or expected version substitution.

requirements.oracle:
Complete source/category admissions and isolated pointer, allocation, coarray, CHARACTER-length and derived-type report/control relations where their independent premises hold. Multilang evidence additionally binds the selected companion, object declarations, source inputs, ordered build/link and defined runtime values.

Batch296 C820 data interop fixtures: Batch296 adds one C companion run for three C820 facets. A module defines an omitted-NAME INTEGER(C_INT) scalar, an explicit NAME scalar, a nonunit-lower-bound explicit-shape INTEGER(C_INT) array, and a separate zero-size INTEGER(C_INT) array with BIND(C). C functions access the same nonzero external objects through independent writes and reads: 11/13 through the omitted default label, 17/19 through the explicit scalar label, and 23/29 then 31/37 through the two nonzero array elements; SIZE(empty_array)=0 checks the zero-size category. Every check uses a literal value independent of the operation that produced it. C-source feature mutations redirect the corresponding companion accessor family to private shadow storage, so the program still compiles and links but the relevant Fortran/C visibility assertion fails at run time.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No unsupported kind, invalid COMMON member, illegal shape declaration, incomplete interface, raw byte layout or undocumented ABI is an oracle. Optional mapping absence is not permission to skip required C_INT behavior or emit success-shaped coverage; unqualified cases remain pending. Source, compiler acceptance, C object compatibility and header/runtime consistency are separate claims.

Batch296 C820 data interop limits: Only guaranteed C_INT scalar and explicit-shape array data, including one zero-size category admission, are covered. No kind code, byte width, storage offset, descriptor, coarray, pointer, allocatable, character kind, derived type, zero-size C counterpart or ABI decoration is inferred. The C source declares the Fortran BIND objects as extern and defines only accessor procedures, so one processor initially defines each linked variable. Other C820 facets remain pending.
requirements.dependencies: 18.2.2;18.3.1 Tables18.1/18.2,18.3.2-.7;7.2 C702;8.2 C808;8.5.8;15.6.2.1 C1563-C1568;18.9.1/.2;19.5.1.5; existing descriptor/c_interop inputs and batch_008 header qualification.

requirements.title: Every member of a BIND common block is interoperable
requirements.definition: Each variable in a common block that has BIND is interoperable. BIND belongs to the block in this condition, not to each member. General COMMON eligibility, same-block storage consistency and the chosen C counterpart remain additional conditions; satisfying a member-wise type test alone does not prove multilang interoperation.

pending.pointer-member-first: PENDING a single complete COMMON declaration with a typed scalar INTEGER(C_INT) data pointer as its first member and an ordinary INTEGER(C_INT) second member. A non-unlimited data pointer is not categorically forbidden by C8123, but is not an interoperable scalar. Repair only removal of POINTER. No pointer value/association is read and no second inconsistent COMMON declaration is supplied.
pending.pointer-member-last: PENDING the same isolated member condition in the last position, with the first member otherwise interoperable. Remove only POINTER for the control. The every-member quantifier must not be replaced by testing only the first member or the block name.
pending.sequence-type-member-source-use: PENDING a complete COMMON-eligible SEQUENCE type with one INTEGER(C_INT) component and no default initialization, versus the corresponding BIND(C) type form with SEQUENCE removed. C8124 and C1801 require this coordinated representation-form change. Keep it source-qualified until the exact focused repair and report are independently established; no non-SEQUENCE non-BIND type falsely offered as an otherwise valid COMMON negative.
pending.character-member-domain: PENDING only with supported C_CHAR: a common block of two fixed-length CHARACTER members, one LEN1 and the other LEN2, with a LEN2-to1 repair. Preserve ordinary COMMON type/storage conditions and complete corresponding declarations. Missing C_CHAR mapping or an unrelated source/length-kind failure cannot corroborate C821.
pending.common-form-exclusions-source-use: PENDING original C8121-C8125 and8.10.2.4 inventory: no individually BIND member, allocatable member/ultimate component, coarray, enumeration-type object, prohibited dummy/result or invalid derived type. Typed-pointer compatibility across declarations remains8.10.2.4p7. Do not re-own these independently illegal COMMON forms as member-interoperability negatives.

requirements.oracle:
Member-specific compile reports and focused repairs distinguish which otherwise valid COMMON member lacks interoperability. Actual C common-block evidence requires the full18.9.1 relationship and compatible typed companion objects; it is not supplied by declaration syntax.

Batch296 C821 common interop fixtures: Batch296 adds one C companion run for two C821 facets. Two INTEGER(C_INT) variables are the only members of one named COMMON block, and BIND(C,NAME='attr_bind_common') is applied to the block, not to either member. A C struct with corresponding first and second int components is accessed through setter/getter procedures: C writes 41/43 and Fortran observes both members, then Fortran writes 47/53 and C observes both members. Feature mutations redirect the C common accessors to private shadow storage, preserving a valid build but breaking the cross-language member checks.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
COMMON obsolescence warnings, unsupported binding implementations, invalid general COMMON membership, layout guesses and missing companion symbols are not interchangeable with this condition. No new fixture, profile, C companion, header selection or approval is supplied by the source plan.

Batch296 C821 common interop limits: Only the finite two-C_INT-member common block is covered. There is no padding, offset, bit-field, union, flexible-array, component-name, obsolescence-warning or duplicate-common declaration oracle. The fixture does not give BIND or SAVE to individual members. Pointer, character, sequence-type and form-exclusion facets remain pending.

requirements.title: A nonblank NAME value denotes a valid companion identifier
requirements.definition: For the supplied scalar default-character constant NAME expression, discard leading and trailing blanks. If the remaining length is nonzero, that value is valid as an identifier on the selected companion processor. This is not a general whitespace normalization, a Fortran-name spelling restriction, an ASCII folding algorithm or an unconditional C compiler/ABI assumption.

pending.blank-trimming: PENDING separate leading-blank, trailing-blank and both-side-blank NAME values around bind_item, with original18.9.2 label interpretation. Remove only Fortran blanks, not tabs, NULs, arbitrary Unicode whitespace or source bytes. A companion runtime equality check remains a separately qualified multilang plan.
pending.valid-companion-identifier: PENDING documented selected-companion identifier rules and two finite ordinary labels bind_item and BindItem in separate qualified contexts. Reserved-name and repertoire conditions belong to the actual companion. An accepted Fortran declaration alone does not establish that selection or identifier validity.
pending.invalid-companion-policy-gate: PENDING source-only candidate labels with a leading digit, embedded blank or punctuation, each repaired to bind_item. They become negative expectations only after the selected companion's actual identifier rules and an independent Fortran reporting policy or canonical duty are established. No mandatory prose rejection or inference from an assembler/linker's ability to represent a symbol.
pending.empty-blank-outside-premise: PENDING NAME='' and all-blank NAME values: no nonzero identifier is tested, and18.9.2 specifies no binding label. NAME is still syntactically present for C802/C877. Do not substitute the entity's default label, demand an empty C identifier or expect a forced link failure.
pending.case-and-default-labels: PENDING18.9.2 source-use of omitted NAME yielding the entity name with lower-case letters, explicit mixed-case labels remaining case significant, and independent Fortran identifier names. Use one collision-free mixed-case companion object per future runtime context; reconcile19.2 before any case-only multi-label program. Neither platform prefixes nor byte-code case arithmetic are standard label semantics.
pending.repertoire-interface-gate: PENDING the original NOTE's finite documentary intersection of companion identifier repertoire and the Fortran default-CHARACTER representation. A permitted companion identifier unavailable in that representation cannot be conjured by nondefault CHARACTER, UTF-8 byte substitution or a display-shape assertion. Keep the interface limitation explicit rather than fabricate an executable example.

requirements.oracle: Original label/value rules plus actual companion/interface evidence determine applicability. Qualified positive multilang observations can compare independent typed values through an exact label; optional prose diagnostic policy is not silently promoted to a standard requirement.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The source restriction remains real without a mandatory local diagnostic. Empty/all-blank, default-name and explicit-name cases stay distinct, and19.2/18.9.1 global-entity restrictions are not waived by case significance. A missing mapping or interface mechanism leaves the relevant facet pending, not a passing skip or an arbitrary runtime/link-failure oracle.
requirements.dependencies: R808;C802/C877;5.5.7;8.5.5 NOTE;18.9.1/.2;18.10.2 for distinct procedure-label exceptions;19.2/19.5.1.5.

requirements.title: BIND on a common block implies SAVE for that block
requirements.definition: Giving a common block BIND also gives that common block SAVE. Its member retention follows the common-block SAVE rules, and an explicit SAVE of the block may confirm the implication. This is not BIND on each member, explicit SAVE on a member, a new module-variable SAVE rule or proof of C interoperability.

pending.member-save-source-use: PENDING8.5.16p3 propagation of common-block SAVE to each member, together with C862's exclusion of explicit member SAVE and C8123's exclusion of individually bound members. Check both defined members in the retention plan without inventing pointer lifetime or allocation effects.
pending.consistent-common-labels: PENDING exact same binding label in every scope declaring the bound block, and identical permitted storage/type/parameter relationships under8.10.2/18.9.1. Different local member names are not label or C component-name equality requirements. Mismatched labels/layouts are separate source conditions, not a SAVE-effect failure oracle.
pending.module-variable-save-distinction: PENDING source-use contrast with an ordinary module BIND variable, whose SAVE follows8.5.16p4, and with initialization-implied SAVE under8.4. Do not relabel those contexts or existing allocation/entry-capture cases as this bound-common implication.

requirements.oracle: Two complete run/f2023 programs represent only named-common-retention and explicit-save-confirmation. The effect program's main calls two external procedures through matching complete explicit interfaces. Only the actual writer and reader declare /saved_pair/, each with two ordinary scalar INTEGER(C_INT) members in identical order and BIND(C) on the block. Main defines typed inputs11/13, calls the writer to completion, then calls the reader and checks both returned values against independent literals. A second complete cycle uses17/19. Main's executable-initialized writer/reader counters are updated inside the corresponding procedures; four visit checks precede value reads, two cycle checks and a ten-check completion guard reject missing visits/checks. Eleven scalar guards plus the exact stdout 'BIND COMMON SAVE OK\n', empty stderr and normal exit0 constitute the run contract. The positive-control program differs only by one inserted SAVE /saved_pair/ in each of the two common-declaring scopes. Original8.5.5p3 expressly permits that confirmation; only its facet is designated positive_control_facets, not effect evidence. Full-program one-span wrong-oracle probes target every guard and the completion literal, using only processors that actually execute the current parent.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The three member-save-source-use, consistent-common-labels and module-variable-save-distinction facets remain pending; all six other8.5.5requirements are preserved. Main, modules and interface bodies declare no common storage. Neither program has declaration/DATA/default initialization, pointer, allocatable, coarray, equivalence, extra common scope or member BIND/SAVE. The effect source has no explicit SAVE; the control has exactly two block SAVE confirmations, never duplicate or member SAVE. Both scopes use the same default binding label and type/order/size; C_INT is guaranteed and imported in each actual/interface scope. Writer assignments define both members before the first read; SAVE preserves their definition/value across complete returns. Counter actuals are defined and distinct, and reader OUT actuals are assigned before any use. No unsaved negative, undefined-value trap, physical static-allocation/address oracle, guessed kind/width, C counterpart or ABI/linkage claim is supplied. The build links only Fortran program units. Normal-zero exit is the existing observation convention; ERROR STOP token/status behavior is qualified empirically, not a mandated numeric exit policy. Compilation/link failures do not qualify runtime sensitivity; actual unsupported/resource/runtime failures remain failures. Source, fixture, mode-qualified observations and inventory approval are separate. Generation changes no review, baseline, source-use or canonical-link record.

review_rationale: Batch296 bound reference-validated attribute fixtures after two review rounds with union-preserving shared oracle text; one frozen-LFortran ICE (CONTIGUOUS assumed-rank dummy) was independently confirmed as genuine.
